<Video 1> is the original source video and the absolute authority for frame order, duration, playback direction, camera position and movement, lens perspective, crop, foreground-subject motion, pose trajectory, gesture timing, body mechanics, screen position, scale, depth, occlusion, focus, motion blur, and foreground geometry. Start from frame 0 of <Video 1> and reproduce the source action forward without skipping ahead, reversing, looping, adding pre-roll, adding post-roll, or retiming.

<Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, and <Picture 3> are three identical copies of the replacement-background reference. Together they are the absolute authority for the visible background environment. Use only their scenery, architecture, vegetation, sky, terrain, colors, materials, illumination character, and background atmosphere. Ignore and never transfer any person, animal, foreground object, pose, framing, crop, or camera from these pictures.

[SWAP_INSTRUCTION]

Treat the running soldier, his face, hair, skin, body, uniform, tactical gear, rifle, hands, limbs, shadows, contacts, silhouette, motion blur, and the foreground grass as immutable foreground from <Video 1>. Replace the original tree line, original sky, and all distant scenery behind the foreground boundary with the background environment defined by <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, and <Picture 3>. The original background must not remain visible.

The replacement background must be clearly established in the first output frame and remain temporally stable through the original final frame. Adapt it to <Video 1>'s camera perspective, parallax, depth, focus, exposure, and motion blur without sliding, swimming, flickering, morphing, or crossing over the soldier or rifle. <Video 1> wins for foreground, timing, camera, geometry, depth, and occlusion boundary. The three pictures win for every replaceable background pixel. Stop at the original source frame count.

Replace only the complete distant background behind the running soldier and foreground grass with the environment from <Picture 1>, duplicated as <Picture 2> and <Picture 3> for stronger background adherence. Remove the original trees, original sky, and original distant scenery from every output frame. Keep the soldier, face, body, uniform, tactical gear, rifle, hands, limbs, pose, running motion, timing, scale, screen position, silhouette, contacts, shadows, motion blur, and foreground grass unchanged. Do not transfer any person or foreground object from the background-reference pictures.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.
